Abstract: In contemporary times, traditional marketing methods have transformed, giving way to online marketing approaches that necessitate internet connectivity. Nevertheless, one of the primary issues faced by firms in the realm of Internet marketing pertains to the identification of appropriate target consumers. This is because if organizations mistakenly target consumers not aligned with their products or services, it can result in ineffective marketing efforts and waste of resources. This research thoroughly examines ad click prediction and classification through a machine learning (ML)-based novel approach. Predictive models are developed by utilizing past ad interaction data, encompassing user demographics, ad features, and contextual information. Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a disruptive force in digital marketing and advertising in the Philippines, transforming how brands plan, execute, and engage with their audiences. This study explores the impact of AI technologies such as automated targeting, personalized content delivery, and campaign optimization on industry practices and professional skillsets. Using the Task Technology Fit (TTF) Model and sentiment analysis, the research identifies a growing dependence on AI tools alongside significant challenges. These include a shortage of AI-related training opportunities, limited institutional support, and ethical concerns related to privacy and algorithmic bias. Despite these obstacles, there is cautious optimism among marketing professionals regarding AI’s potential to enhance creativity, efficiency, and strategic decision-making. The findings emphasize the importance of developing human-AI collaboration frameworks, strengthening ethical standards, and promoting AI literacy across sectors. Collaboration among educational institutions, industry leaders, and policymakers is essential to building a resilient and future-ready advertising workforce in the Philippines.

Abstract: Digital marketing i.e., any type of advertising proposed on electronic devices over the Internet, has been the prevalent advertising methodology in the last decades. As such, measuring its effectiveness and distinguishing genuine conversions generated by real users from fraudulent traffic (for example generated by bots) is of utmost importance. In this paper, such issue is tackled by using Machine Learning and, specifically, comparing a Shallow Neural Network and a Random Forest, to automatically classify traffic data of digital marketing campaigns into “good” and “bad” traffic. The two proposed models are evaluated on real traffic data, manually annotated. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed classification task, with the Shallow Neural Network achieving a 98% precision and recall, without exhibiting overfitting, over the 32,000 samples of the tested dataset.

Abstract: The growth of visual content in digital marketing has led to the need to have hyper-personalized campaigns that emulate individual user tastes. To extract hierarchical image features, Smart Visual uses Convolutional Neural Networks (EfficientNet and ResNet) and Transformer-based attention layers to extract semantic and contextual information between marketing images. Publication Title: 2025 8th International Conference of Computer and Informatics Engineering (IC2IE)
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the correlation between buyer perception and the influence of influencer authenticity on customer satisfaction within contemporary skincare digital marketing campaigns. Utilizing a purposive sampling method, data were collected from 253 Indonesian internet users in May 2025, all of whom had previously purchased skincare products based on influencer recommendations. The research examines how buyer perception and influencer trustworthiness influence purchase and repurchase intention. Data analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with the help of Smart-PLS software. The results demonstrate that consumer perception plays a significant role in shaping satisfaction, which in turn affects repurchase intention. Additionally, influencer trustworthiness strongly impacts purchase intention; however, trust alone is insufficient without being supported by consistent and strategic social media advertising. In a competitive and saturated skincare market, authenticity and transparency in influencer communication are essential for maintaining consumer trust. This study suggests that digital marketing strategies involving credible influences, when paired with effective advertising efforts, can better foster customer satisfaction, engagement, and long-term loyalty. The insights derived from this study offer practical value for skincare brands seeking to refine their influencer marketing strategies and build campaigns aligned with evolving consumer behavior in the digital space.
